source_snapshot.procedure: Use OpenBMC WebUI/Remote Console to mount an HTTPS image and notes that the ISO can later be used for OS installation.
source_snapshot.criteria: Remote Console connects; CD-ROM mounts and an Auto-install program appears.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL but labels inputs HTTP and uses generic block-device evidence.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: BLOCKED for scope, TLS/image identity, disk protection and cleanup.

old_problem: The previous review correctly identified TLS and destructive-install risks but treated ordinary project bindings and the phrase about what media can later be used for as an unresolved core decision.
disposition_reason: The test owns HTTPS retrieval, Remote Console, exact virtual-CD exposure and visible auto-install landing page. It ends before any installer action. The exact URL, CA/authentication policy, image hash and BMC workflow are safe runtime/project prerequisites under ED-36; HTTPS is not downgraded to the HTTP terminology in DeepSeek.
decision_basis: Direct inspection covered XLSX row 747, same-row DeepSeek columns, exact GPT V2 object and historical record.
OpenBMC's official virtual-media design explicitly includes remote HTTPS ISO/IMG retrieval and host exposure as virtual storage.
The source says an installation is something one can do after mounting; the acceptance verb is that the program `show up`, so visibility can be verified without starting it.
ED-35 bars installation credit, ED-31 requires actual visual evidence, and ED-36 moves URL/CA/image values to readiness rather than permanent BLOCKED.

test_case.test_name: Mount a certificate-validated HTTPS image and verify exact virtual-CD and installer visibility
test_case.purpose: Prove the BMC retrieves the approved immutable image through authenticated HTTPS, presents it to the host as the intended virtual optical device, displays its installer/auto-install landing screen, and cleanly removes it without changing boot or disk state.
required_package: Exact HTTPS URL, immutable image hash, content length/type and redirect policy
Trusted CA chain, hostname/time prerequisites and approved authentication/secret-handling method
Isolated SUT with boot and protected-disk baseline plus trusted read-only device tools
test_case.test_command: Pre-validate the HTTPS endpoint certificate chain, hostname, validity time, redirect destination and exact image hash through approved controls. Operator then mounts that URL in the actual BMC WebUI/Remote Console. Agent may capture trusted before/after `lsblk -o NAME,PATH,TYPE,SIZE,RO,FSTYPE,MOUNTPOINTS,MODEL,SERIAL` evidence. Stop at the visible installer/launcher landing page, never choose Install/Next, then eject/deactivate and prove device removal.
test_case.expected_result: TLS validation succeeds without bypass; WebUI identifies the intended HTTPS image as active; Remote Console works; exactly one attributable virtual optical device and the expected installer landing page appear; eject removes it while physical disks, boot configuration and host/BMC health remain unchanged.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires trusted certificate/hostname validation, exact-image identity, actual GUI/console evidence, correlated virtual-device visibility, launcher visibility and cleanup. FAIL includes TLS/redirect/auth failure, wrong or mutable content, device mismatch, console error, unexpected boot/write, or residual media. No OS-installation result may be inferred.
safety_gate: Never disable TLS/hostname verification, silently follow an unapproved redirect, or log/embed credentials in the URL
Reject image hash/content mismatch and mount read-only where supported
No boot-order change, installer continuation, partitioning or physical-disk write
Keep independent recovery console and stop on automatic installer advance or any storage mutation; no automatic retry
Always deactivate media and verify removal
expected_evidence: Redacted URL/auth policy, CA chain/hostname/validity and redirect record
Image hash/content metadata and BMC/WebUI version
Actual WebUI/Remote Console screenshots through mounted and visible-launcher states
Before/mounted/ejected device inventories, unchanged boot/storage state and health logs
test_case.recovery: If trust, media identity or console state is unexpected, do not proceed. Preserve evidence and deactivate. If a boot/installer transition occurs, do not confirm prompts; use the independent console to eject media and restore only the approved boot baseline, then escalate before reboot or retry.

source_conflict.preserved_original_conflict: Master wording mixes HTTP labels with an HTTPS URL, incomplete numbering and possible later installation.
source_conflict.resolution: HTTPS semantics control; observable launcher visibility ends this test, while actual install remains separate.

blocked.reason: Transport, endpoint, evidence and recovery are bounded. CA, URL and image values are readiness inputs.
